Hypothesis: We hypothesize that EGCG-rich green tea catechins, by recognizing and binding to CSC-specific mitochondrial membrane components and enzyme profiles, selectively impair mitochondrial oxidative phosphorylation in cancer stem cells. Simultaneously, EGCG modulates crucial survival signals by attenuating IL-8 and PI3K/AKT pathways. This dual mechanism results in severe metabolic stress, triggering the intrinsic apoptotic cascade and inhibiting CSC self-renewal. Leveraging advanced techniques such as high-resolution respirometry, single-cell metabolomics, mitochondrial proteomics, and single-cell RNA sequencing, we aim to distinguish these effects in CSCs from non-cancer stem cell populations, thereby establishing a refined, targeted strategy to mitigate metastasis and recurrence.
Abstract: We propose that EGCG-rich green tea catechins selectively reprogram the energy metabolism of cancer stem cells (CSCs) by targeting their distinct mitochondrial molecular signatures while concurrently modulating IL-8 and PI3K/AKT signaling pathways. This dual mode of action, refined by contemporary single-cell omics and imaging-based metabolic analyses, leads to targeted disruption of mitochondrial oxidative phosphorylation in CSCs, inflicting critical energy depletion and metabolic stress. Consequently, intrinsic apoptotic pathways are activated, self-renewal is inhibited, and selective elimination of CSCs is achieved, potentially preventing metastasis and disease recurrence. Our integrated approach employs high-resolution respirometry, single-cell metabolomics, mitochondrial proteomics, and single-cell RNA sequencing to map these effects at subcellular resolution and confirm CSC-specific vulnerability relative to non-CSC tumor populations.
CausalChain: EGCG-rich green tea catechins -> Exploitation of CSC-specific mitochondrial membrane compositions and enzyme profiles + Modulation of IL-8 and PI3K/AKT signaling -> Selective disruption of mitochondrial oxidative phosphorylation in CSCs -> Energy depletion and metabolic stress -> Activation of intrinsic apoptotic pathways -> Inhibition of self-renewal -> Selective elimination of CSCs -> Prevention of metastasis and recurrence
